correctness.rationale: For a two-terminal multi-theta graph with m>=3 internally disjoint paths of lengths ell_i>=2, equal indegree parity of orientations is equivalent to flipping an even subset of whole paths, the binary cycle-space fiber of size 2^(m-1); global parity supplies exactly 2^(|V|-1) feasible signatures. Coherence of each path is fiber invariant. A directed cycle occurs iff two coherent paths point opposite ways. For a proper coherent-path set S, number of fibers B_S=2 product_{i notin S}(2^(ell_i-1)-1), and each fiber has h_m(|S|) acyclic representatives, h=2^(m-1) for r<=1 else 2^(m-r). All-coherent orientations form two fibers; for odd m each holds one acyclic orientation, for even m one holds two and the unique other (all-odd indegree signature) none. This yields the stated polynomial and its derivative total, 2 prod_i(2^ell_i-1)-prod_i(2^ell_i-2). Independent brute orientation/acyclicity groupings reproduce five small length patterns; these do not replace the cycle-space/coherence proof.
residual_risks: Bounded independent tests do not prove any unbounded theorem; the written proof was reconstructed and tested against boundary assumptions.

originality.rationale: General parity-orientation work addresses existence of an acyclic representative, not the count spectrum within every feasible signature. Multi-path acyclic polynomial of Mühlherr–Poullot is indexed by edge-direction disagreement relative to a reference orientation, a scalar different from vertex indegree-parity signature. Existing Resultary work on acyclic orientation signatures for complete graphs minus a matching uses a different graph and another statistic. The exact parity-fiber histogram is additional and not implied merely by existence or the global acyclic-orientation total.
residual_risks: Literature may contain a hidden exact parity-fiber count under a different encoding; searches are not exhaustive.
Domain requires m>=3 and ell_i>=2; neither arbitrary series-parallel graphs nor multigraph parallel edges is covered.

value.rationale: The theorem is a natural complete classification of parity constrained acyclic orientations on a series-parallel graph family with overlapping cycles. It sharpens a qualitative source/non-source obstruction into an explicit signature multiplicity spectrum, and locates the unique nonrealizable all-odd signature when m even. This is mathematically motivated despite elementary counting.
residual_risks: Exact finite/general value rests on intrinsic mathematical motivation, not reproducibility alone.
